description.p: Add experimental CPU Parakeet recognition and quick selection of prepared models and languages. Keep each dictation on its starting settings. Replace the experimental Flatpak build with a portable x86_64 AppImage; DEB and RPM remain available.
Include the reliability improvements from 0.7.2 and correct the update metadata regression test on build hosts without package authorization tools.

Improve concurrent settings saves, Unicode dictionary matching, recording cancellation and worker resource limits. Preserve malformed configuration files, retain package transaction ownership, and report partial model deletion accurately.

Microphone selection, a short level check without audio storage, and optional recording sounds. A local personal dictionary adds whole-phrase text replacements with a draft preview and an enable switch.

Optional hold-to-talk with desktop portal press and release events, direct access to the indicator, and opt-in update checks with an update notice on the main page. Linux-wide application descriptions and expanded interface screenshots.

In-app package updates with automatic interface restart and recovery, a compact status card and convenient keyboard shortcuts. Improved cancellation, localization, recognizer output limits and release validation.
A more compact dictation card, collapsible first-use guidance, Linux package descriptions and AppStream screenshots. Runtime preparation and native package updates now exclude each other.

First-run language and model setup, KDE shortcut configuration, a compact movable indicator, native package updates, and ten interface languages with Arabic RTL. Improved configuration recovery, service ownership and package removal.
Reliable Fedora image pulls, acknowledged clipboard delivery and simpler UI background completion with corrected engine tooltips.
Improved model download state, unsaved settings protection, first-use guidance and diagnostic export; added recognition presets, an optional status indicator and Fedora RPM packages.

Improved recording cleanup, cancellation, worker recovery and daemon readiness. Local recognition uses explicit offline model snapshots. Dictation text is hidden in notifications unless enabled in settings. The UI is decomposed into owned controllers and pages. Native and Flatpak share pinned runtime dependencies; repeated Debian builds on the same toolchain use reproducible source timestamps.

Test-suite portability fix: a test class without a skip guard errored on machines without GTK bindings and turned CI red at the 0.6.4 commit; the release gate now also runs the suite with GTK imports blocked. A Hub model whose download helper is missing from a damaged install is reported as an error naming the repair instead of "this model cannot be downloaded". While the model loads into memory, the main window says "Preparing" rather than a finished transfer at 100%.

Fixed: the Download button silently did nothing when the Faster-Whisper runtime was not prepared. The daemon reported "this model cannot be downloaded" about a model that only lacked its fetcher, the window hid the row and the button, and the press did nothing visible. A missing runtime is now an error that names the setup step (Settings or wayvoice engine-setup), the failed row stays visible, the button returns for the same model, and a refusal from the daemon appears as a toast. Fixed: the main window kept saying "Press and speak" while the model was being downloaded or loaded into memory; it now names the model, shows the download progress, and says when the weights are being read in.

Post-release hardening: the daemon no longer loses its warm worker (a stale worker identity could leave an invisible worker holding the model while every dictation loaded from scratch), and one wrong value in config.json can no longer disable model preparation for the rest of the session — every numeric setting has a floor, the preparation thread clears its state whatever happens, and a cancellation is reported as cancelled rather than as an error. Deleting a model can no longer damage files shared with another model (per-file keep logic, recursive snapshot walk, consistent path normalization). Copying logs no longer freezes the window, long toasts are clipped, concurrent dependency installs are serialized and cannot hang on a package that asks a question, and Ctrl-C during an install no longer leaves the package manager holding the dpkg lock. A package built without the bundled ydotool no longer restarts its helper every two seconds, the restart budget is real (60 s window in the unit's [Unit] section), and the first dictation after an install pastes. Numbers, times, file names and URLs survive punctuation. The Debian package now declares the build host's architecture instead of all, and a malformed max_recording_sec is reported even when the recognition engine is not yet prepared.

Automatic pasting works again after installing into a session that was already open: the daemon starts the ydotoold helper itself when nothing answers on its socket, and a failed paste says why and writes the reason to the service log. One notification per dictation, updated as the state changes. Automatic pasting works on distributions that do not package ydotool: the helper is built from vendored sources and shipped with the package, and a distribution's own copy is still preferred. Licence is AGPL-3.0-or-later.

Model management with a visible, cancellable download, all 100 recognition languages, an engine registry, a warm worker that loads the model when the daemon starts, and a daemon that starts with or without systemd.
License metadata aligned to GPL-3.0-only across the About dialog, packaging metadata and AppStream data.
Localization, safer transcription, GNOME-style icon, diagnostics and GitHub project infrastructure.
